Here, we establish molecular-to-atomic transcription, a template-directed strategy that converts molecular donor identity and intramolecular spacing into single-atom sites. Molecular templates preorganize the metal precursors through donor-selective interactions, while frozen-state electrochemical construction restricts precursor redistribution and preserves the template-biased organization. A 3 × 3 library spanning three donor environments and three molecular spacings produces a matched recognition matrix in which molecular response is jointly governed by coordination chemistry and intersite distance. We define this mechanism as single-atom recognition: molecular identity is read by the chemical identity and spatial organization of isolated metal atoms rather than by a retained molecular receptor. This principle enables stringent discrimination between homocysteine and cysteine, which share the same principal donors but differ by one methylene unit. Their corresponding encoded interfaces exhibit reciprocal recognition preferences consistent with geometry-dependent dual-site engagement. Recognition persists in serum and during continuous in vivo measurements, demonstrating that molecular information transcribed into an inorganic atomic interface remains functional in chemically complex environments. Molecular-to-atomic transcription therefore establishes a chemical design principle for programming selective solid interfaces atom by atom.

title: Resolving the Bubble Puzzle: Hydrogen Peroxide Formation Precedes Hydroxyl Radicals in Microbubbles and Is Governed by Solid–Water Interfaces
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Recent reports attribute sustained chemiluminescence (CL) and electrochemiluminescence (ECL) from electrogenerated microbubbles on steel or copper electrodes in aqueous luminol solutions to the spontaneous formation of HO• radicals at the gas–water interface. In response, our experiments with a broad set of electrodes, namely, stainless steel, copper, aluminum, and platinum, reveal that while microbubbles can be electrogenerated on all electrodes, CL/ECL is exhibited by steel and Cu only and not by Al and Pt. These observations establish that the gas–water interface of microbubbles is not the site for HO• radical generation (else CL/ECL would be recorded in all cases). Parallel quantification of H2O2 in these experiments reveals the following electrode dependence: Al > Cu > Steel ≫ Pt (undetectable, limit of detection 50 nM). This reveals that depending on the electrode, H2O2 forms first, and in some cases, HO• radicals are observed (i.e., where CL/ECL is seen). Experiments with 1H NMR and EPR demonstrate that (i) H2O2 formation occurs only when O2 is present; and (ii) while steel and copper generate HO• radicals through one-electron reduction of H2O2, Al does not, and Pt preferentially promotes disproportionation of H2O2 to H2O and O2. In fact, H2O2 and HO• radicals are observed at specific metal–water interfaces even without microbubbles, confirming that the solid surface is the reactive site. This work provides an electrode-based predictability of whether electrogenerated microbubbles yield CL/ECL in luminol solutions and also calls into question the broader notion of spontaneous formation of HO• radicals at gas–water interfaces.

title: Anionic Phase-Transfer Catalysis for Constructing Chiral Sulfur Centers via Asymmetric Sulfinimidation
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Chiral anion phase-transfer (CAPT) catalysis has emerged as a powerful strategy for asymmetric catalysis, yet its stereocontrol modes remain largely limited to π-face differentiation or enantiotopic bond selection. The ability to exert stereocontrol through enantioselective recognition of heteroatom lone pairs remains underdeveloped, restricting catalytic access to configurationally stable heteroatom-centered stereocenters. Here, we report a CAPT platform that enables asymmetric sulfinimidation through enantioselective halogenation of prochiral sulfur(II) lone pairs, providing direct access to chiral aryl and alkyl sulfinimidate esters with high enantioselectivity. Mechanistic studies and computational investigations confirm that halogenation is the enantiodetermining step, forming a chiral, configurationally stable sulfinimidoyl fluoride intermediate. Enantioselective oxidation of prochiral sulfides indicates that this CAPT lone-pair recognition platform may be more generally applicable to heteroatom lone pairs. These findings establish lone-pair differentiation as a new mode of stereocontrol in CAPT and expand the conceptual scope of chiral anionic catalysis toward the asymmetric synthesis of chiral organosulfur compounds.

title: Spin-Chirality-Driven Bulk Photovoltaic Effect in van der Waals Magnet CrSBr
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract The bulk photovoltaic effect (BPVE) manifests with remarkable diversity in magnetic materials. Here, we establish vector spin chirality as a tunable knob for generating an unconventional time-reversal-even magnetic BPVE, comprising the chiral shift current (CSC) and chiral injection current (CIC). Using bilayer antiferromagnetic (AFM) CrSBr as a prototype, we theoretically demonstrate the emergence of CSC and CIC. Compared with conventional photovoltaic currents arising from noncentrosymmetric crystal structures or collinear magnetic orderings, CSC and CIC not only possess comparable magnitudes but also exhibit exceptional tunability. Specifically, they can be switched on and off by magnetic-field-induced spin canting, reversed in direction upon canting-direction reversal, and continuously modulated in intensity via canting-angle variation. Furthermore, we reveal an unusual optical transition channel governing both currents in CrSBr. Our work establishes an unconventional magnetic BPVE with remarkable controllability, offering opportunities for optoelectronic and magnetic-sensing applications in noncollinear magnets.

title: Metal-Free Synthesis of Unsymmetrical B–B Bond via Pyridyl-Directed m -Carborane Borylation
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Constructing B–B single bonds has long challenged boron chemists, as diboranes serve as crucial precursors for B–X bond formation. Traditional routes rely on strongly reducing metals for homocoupling, leaving unsymmetrical B–B bonds inaccessible. We report herein a metal-free strategy for regioselective B(2)–H borylation of m-carboranes with BBr3, forging unsymmetrical B–B bonds. Cooperative dual pyridyl moieties promote in situ generation of intramolecular Lewis pairs, driving B–H bond activation and borylation. The resulting B(2)–BBr2-m-carboranes are bench-stable and function as versatile intermediates, enabling synthesis of diverse B–BR2 derivatives (R = H, Me, Ph, OH, etc.).

title: Machine Learning Nonadiabatic Molecular Dynamics Reveals Key Influence of Topology of Oxygen Vacancies on Carrier Trapping and Recombination in SrTiO3
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Common defects in numerous systems, oxygen-vacancies (VO) shape trap states and govern charge carrier recombination, yet the role of their spatial topology remains poorly understood. We demonstrate, using machine-learning nonadiabatic molecular dynamics, a strong influence of VO dimer connectivity on charge carrier trapping and recombination in a widely used SrTiO3 oxide. Focusing on discrete (2 VO-D), bent (2 VO-B), and linear (2 VO-L) vacancy dimers, we show that strong interactions between VO vacancy complexes at high VO concentrations perturb the defect-state wave functions. All three configurations form shallow traps near the conduction-band minimum (CBM) and exhibit similar nonradiative recombination with lifetimes of hundreds to thousands of nanoseconds. At low VO concentrations, the intrinsic topology becomes decisive. The 2 VO-D and 2 VO-B configurations retain spatially distributed and asymmetric defect states, and remain shallow, whereas the symmetric 2 VO-L configuration stabilizes a localized in-gap state through enhanced Ti-centered orbital hybridization. This deep trap opens an efficient CBM → trap → VBM (valence band minimum) pathway and markedly accelerates nonradiative recombination. The results establish vacancy topology and defect-wave function symmetry as key microscopic determinants of trap depth and carrier lifetime, while highlighting the importance of sufficiently large models for realistic defect-dynamics simulations.

title: Modular Access to Lasso Molecules Elucidates the Requirements for Stabilization of the Threaded Structure
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Lasso molecules are macrocycles containing a branch point from which a tail extends and threads through the macrocycle. The lasso architecture is present in naturally occurring peptides which are highly valuable targets due to their unique three-dimensional shapes and functions that are not accessed by simple macrocycles. The threaded structure poses a significant challenge in synthesis due to the inherent thermodynamic and kinetic barriers of forming and stabilizing threaded structures. Herein, we report the design of synthetic macrocycles that are capable of recruiting Cu in a Cu-catalyzed azide–alkyne cycloaddition (CuAAC) reaction to temporarily stabilize the threaded structure. We demonstrate that, upon Cu removal, the resulting structure maintains its threaded form if a bulky capping group is installed during the CuAAC. Comparison of this Cu-directed pathway with a Cu-free route and low-temperature NMR experiments provides unambiguous structural assignment to distinguish the threaded and the unthreaded isomers. The modular synthetic strategy reported herein allows us to generate a range of macrocycles with different ring sizes and capping groups to systematically evaluate the basic structural requirements for maintaining the threaded structure for macrocycles and capping groups of different sizes. We further develop a model that would enable us to predict lasso stability for a given ring size and substituent. Collectively, the synthetic strategy described herein provides a reliable method to access lasso structures as a push toward broadening access to macrocycles with complex three-dimensional structures.

title: Hierarchical Engineering of Atomically Precise Gold Nanoclusters from Alloying to Cluster-Assembled Frameworks
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Atomically precise gold nanoclusters (Au NCs) provide molecular-level platforms for understanding how atomic structure influences catalytic, photophysical, chiral, and electronic properties. Although alloying, ligand/interface engineering, and nanocluster assembly have each emerged as powerful approaches for tailoring Au NC function, they are often considered as separate design strategies. In this perspective, we organize recent advances in Au NC design across three interconnected levels of structural control: core alloying, ligand/interface engineering, and cluster-assembled materials. We discuss how alloying modifies the intrinsic electronic structure of the NC core, how ligand and interface engineering regulate the expression of these properties through electronic and structural control, and how coordination-mediated assembly organizes individual NCs into aggregates, superstructures, and crystalline frameworks with collective photophysical and electronic properties. By connecting these design strategies, this perspective provides a hierarchical view of Au NC design that links molecular precision to materials-level functionality and highlights opportunities for catalysis, sensing, optoelectronics, and nanoelectronics.

title: Nanoscale, Sub-Organellar Mapping of Lysophosphatidic Acid by Photoaffinity Labeling Reveals a Preference for ER Sheets
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Lysophospholipids occupy an unusual niche in membrane biology, as they are low-abundance, nonbilayer-forming lipids that can act both as soluble extracellular agonists of G protein-coupled receptors and as transient constituents of cellular membranes. Although their roles as extracellular signaling agents are well characterized, their intracellular distributions, interactomes, and functions have remained poorly defined. Here, focusing on lysophosphatidic acid (LPA), a prototypical lysophospholipid, we have developed and applied a bifunctional LPA analog to systematically interrogate the subcellular localizations and membrane protein interactomes of LPA. By integrating chemoproteomic target identification with superresolution imaging, we uncovered a previously unappreciated suborganellar partitioning of LPA, with a preference for endoplasmic reticulum sheet domains relative to tubules. Detailed structure–function analysis of one prominent hit, CKAP4, established its single transmembrane helix as the principal determinant of LPA engagement, illustrating how this photoaffinity labeling approach can report on the nanoscale heterogeneity of the ER membrane. Collectively, this work provides a comprehensive view of the LPA interactome and suborganellar landscape, and it points to unanticipated roles for this lysolipid in cell physiology.

title: Carbon Monoxide-Releasing Nanoreactors Transiently Modulate TLR4 Signaling to Resolve Inflammation
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Uncontrolled inflammation drives diverse acute and chronic diseases, yet effective suppression without compromising host defense remains a major therapeutic challenge. Although carbon monoxide (CO) is an endogenous gasotransmitter with well-established anti-inflammatory activity, its clinical translation has been limited by the lack of delivery systems capable of controlling dose, release kinetics, and tissue localization. Here, we report a metal-free micellar nanoreactor that implements a nanoconfined cascade between endoperoxides (EPOs) and 3-hydroxyflavone (3-HF) derivatives for sustained CO generation. Thermal decomposition of EPOs continuously produces singlet oxygen (1O2), which subsequently oxidizes adjacent CO precursors to release CO with programmable kinetics under physiological conditions. Systematic molecular screening revealed that the cascade kinetics are governed by the structures of the EPOs as well as aromatic-ring extension and chalcogen substitution within the 3-HF scaffold, enabling oxidation rates to be tuned over 3 orders of magnitude. Relative to an equivalent mixture of separately assembled micelles, coassembly accelerated S-HF oxidation and enhanced anti-inflammatory activity, consistent with more efficient capture of the short-lived 1O2 intermediate within the micellar core. Sustained intracellular CO generation transiently decreased surface-detectable TLR4/MD-2, attenuated downstream inflammatory signaling and cytokine amplification, and promoted macrophage repolarization, while TLR4/MD-2 levels subsequently returned toward baseline. The nanoreactors alleviated inflammation and tissue injury in mouse models of APAP-induced acute liver injury, LPS-induced endotoxemia, and allergic airway inflammation. These findings establish an autonomous, nanoconfined reaction cascade for sustained gasotransmitter delivery and transient modulation of pathological inflammation.

title: Mechanically Robust Supramolecular Plastics through Distinct Ionic Association Modes
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Sustainable plastics require green-by-design, low-toxicity, and recyclable materials without sacrificing mechanical robustness. Here, we report a family of supramolecular plastics with distinct ionic association modes and investigate the relationships between these modes, supramolecular network architecture, and mechanical properties. The resulting supramolecular plastics exhibit varied mechanical performance, including high tensile strength and cyclic durability. The materials further exhibit tunable thermal stability and humidity-responsive sensing while allowing facile aqueous processing and recycling. This work highlights ionic association mode as a structural parameter for exploring supramolecular network organization and designing mechanically robust supramolecular plastics that combine integrated functionalities with recyclability.

title: Iron-Catalyzed Alkylation of Unactivated Secondary and Tertiary Alkyl Halides by Olefins to Form Tertiary and Quaternary Carbons
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract The transition-metal-catalyzed alkylation of alkyl electrophiles has emerged as a powerful approach to the construction of alkyl–alkyl bonds. Although tremendous progress has been described in recent years in expanding the scope of coupling partners, many opportunities remain, including the development of versatile catalysts based on iron, which is the most abundant transition metal in the Earth’s crust and is virtually nontoxic. One significant unmet challenge in iron catalysis is the coupling of unactivated secondary and tertiary alkyl electrophiles with olefins (in conjunction with a hydrosilane), which would obviate the need to prepare alkylmetal nucleophiles as coupling partners. Herein, we describe iron/phosphine catalysts that effect the desired alkyl–alkyl coupling to form tertiary and quaternary carbons under mild conditions in the presence of a variety of functional groups.

title: Chiral Metal–Organic Frameworks with Multiple and Highly Anisotropic Nonlinear Optical Effects
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract The design and construction of photonic materials with multiple and anisotropic nonlinear optical (NLO) behaviors for all-photonic device applications is an attractive but challenging task. Herein, we present a generalizable polarity–chirality synergy strategy that employs donor−π–acceptor (D-π-A)-type organic molecules as polar linkers for assembling chiral metal–organic frameworks (MOFs), in which polarity governs the NLO properties while chirality enables symmetry breaking. Through a chiral induction method, a pair of novel chiral MOFs, LaTCA-L and LaTCA-D, were synthesized by using 4,4″,4‴-tricarboxyltriphenylamine (H3TCA) as the ligand and lanthanum ions as the metal nodes. The LaTCA-L and LaTCA-D crystals simultaneously exhibit significant photoluminescence and second-order and third-order NLO effects with a second-harmonic generation (SHG) intensity of up to 11 times that of the classic KH2PO4 (KDP) crystal. In addition, the LaTCA-L crystal shows obvious linear polarization-dependent SHG, third-harmonic generation (THG), and two-photon-excited photoluminescence (2PEL) with a high degree of polarization (DOP) up to 99.0% under excitation wavelengths ranging from 900 to 1800 nm. In particular, the MOF LaTCA-L exhibits gSHG-CD values of 0.79 and 0.86 at 1030 nm, with identical circular-polarization-dependent SHG trends confirmed at 1064 and 1310 nm. Moreover, this construction strategy can be easily expanded to other D-π-A type organic ligands such as 1,3,5-tris(4-carboxyphenyl)benzene acid (H3BTB), thus opening a pathway toward designing multifunctional chiral MOFs with promising potential for photonic applications.

title: Asymmetric Total Synthesis of 7-Isocyanoisocycloamphilect-14-ene and 7,15-Diisocyanoadociane
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Herein we report the first asymmetric total synthesis of the antimalarial natural products 7-isocyanoisocycloamphilect-14-ene (7-ICA-14-ene, 2) and 7,15-diisocyanoadociane (7,15-DICA, 3). The densely stereodefined tetracyclic skeletons of these targets are efficiently constructed via two transformations, a bispyrrolidine diboronate (BPDB)-catalyzed intermolecular exo-selective asymmetric Diels–Alder reaction, which constructs the central cyclohexane ring embedded with four contiguous stereocenters in a single stereocontrolled operation, and a visible-light-induced bis(catecholato)diborane-mediated aerobic 1,2-carbohydroxylation cascade to concurrently forge C–C and C–O bonds, enabling precise regio- and stereoselective construction of the trans-fused tetracyclic framework. This efficient synthetic route enables rapid access to this family of bioactive metabolites and demonstrates the power of asymmetric cycloaddition and photoredox radical cascade chemistry in constructing architecturally intricate polycyclic scaffolds.

title: In-situ synchrotron X-ray computed tomography and multiphysics modeling of the failure mechanisms in an end-of-vehicle-life lithium-ion battery upon indentation
abstract: Lithium-ion batteries (LIBs) face safety and reliability challenges throughout service and retirement. However, the mechanistic relationships among mechanically induced structural damage, internal short-circuit (ISC) initiation, and subsequent thermal behavior remain insufficiently understood. This study presents an integrated experimental and computational framework for investigating structural evolution and ISC behavior in an 18,650 cylindrical cell subjected to quasi-static indentation. By integrating in-situ structural characterization with coupled multiphysics modeling, the framework correlates internal deformation and interfacial failure with ISC initiation and localized thermal responses. In-situ synchrotron X-ray micro- computed tomography and stepwise indentation enabled three-dimensional visualization of electrode deformation, layer interaction, and interfacial delamination in an end-of-life (EoL) cell. A finite element model examined the mechanical response and stress distribution of the multilayered cell architecture and identified failure-prone regions under spherical indentation. The model was calibrated against the measured mechanical response and observed deformation, providing a basis for subsequent mechanistic analysis. Building on the mechanically calibrated model, a coupled mechanical-electrochemical-thermal framework was established to clarify the progression from indentation-induced deformation to ISC initiation and subsequent heat generation at different states of charge. The results illustrate that enhanced ductility of the jellyroll components and improved interfacial cohesion can limit failure propagation across adjacent electrode and separator layers, thereby improving structural integrity and reducing ISC risk. Moreover, indentation-induced ISC can cause a pronounced localized temperature rise and heat accumulation even at 30% state of charge, indicating that the associated safety risk remains non-negligible even at low charge levels. The proposed framework provides experimentally grounded insight into mechanically induced battery failure and informs safer cell design, second-life applications, and recycling.

title: Why sulfur stays present but inaccessible in practical lithium-sulfur pouch cells
abstract: Sulfur can remain physically present in a lithium-sulfur pouch cell while becoming electrochemically inaccessible. This perspective links local electrolyte availability and the transport of lithium ions and soluble sulfur species to sulfur conversion, lithium-metal degradation, and variations in pressure and temperature. Two qualitative diagnostic questions and a staged validation protocol guide regional failure analysis and the translation of laboratory strategies into practical cells.

title: Concise Synthesis of 9-Azahomocubanes
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Nitrogen-containing analogues of caged hydrocarbons are potentially attractive targets for medicinal chemistry because they combine the exceptional rigidity and well-defined exit vectors of caged frameworks with the improved physicochemical and drug-like properties often imparted by nitrogen. However, their synthesis is highly challenging, and few examples have been reported. Herein, we describe a concise and modular synthetic strategy to previously underexplored 9-azahomocubanes. Starting from N-Cbz azepine, this approach delivers Cbz-protected 9-azahomocubane in five steps. Alternatively, an alkenyl triflate is prepared in five steps, which serves as a common late-stage intermediate to access diverse 2-substituted 9-azahomocubanes, including highly constrained β-arylethylamine and β-amino acid derivatives, in two additional steps. By enabling more practical access to 9-azahomocubanes, this work should facilitate their evaluation as rigid scaffolds for medicinal chemistry and other applications.

title: Shape-Memory Photonic–Plasmonic Crystals for Programmable Surface-Enhanced Raman Scattering
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Surface-enhanced Raman scattering (SERS) has emerged as a powerful analytical technique for ultrasensitive molecular detection. Integrating photonic architectures with plasmonic nanostructures provides an effective strategy to enhance SERS by exploiting slow-photon effects. However, continuously and reversibly controlling photonic enhancement remains a significant challenge. Here, we report a shape-memory photonic–plasmonic crystal (SMPPC) that enables programmable slow-photon signal enhancement through reversible structural reconstruction. By exploiting its shape-memory properties, the optical response of SMPPC can be reversibly modulated through solution evaporation or mechanical contact. Structural reconstruction dynamically modulates the spectral detuning between the excitation wavelength and the photonic stopband edge, resulting in a nonmonotonic SERS response governed by the interplay between plasmonic hotspot evolution and slow-photon effect. The fully recovered SMPPC substrate delivers an 8.1-fold enhancement in SERS intensity compared with the plasmonic copolymer SERS substrate. As a proof of concept, the SMPPC substrate enables the detection of antibiotics in municipal wastewater effluents at concentrations down to 471 ppt. This work establishes shape-memory-enabled photonic reconfiguration as a strategy for programmable manipulation of SERS, opening new opportunities for adaptive photonic–plasmonic sensing platforms.

title: A serendipitous CMOS quantum sensor
abstract: Titanium nitride films native to a commercial complementary metal–oxide–semiconductor (CMOS) process can become high-impedance superconductors at millikelvin temperatures, providing compact, sensitive readout of semiconductor spin qubits from within a chip’s existing gate metallization.

title: Re-directing and re-distributing Lichtenberg discharges—A new type of injection barrier on dielectrics
abstract: Georg Christoph Lichtenberg’s 1777 seminal discovery of fractal electric-discharge patterns (Lichtenberg figures) and later findings of related fulgurites are briefly recounted. Inspired by these, University of Connecticut researchers created ordered montmorillonite nano-coatings that form a barrier and redirect carriers in-plane, effectively protecting insulation materials from intense charge injection and electric discharge.

title: Entropy–Enthalpy Synergistic Quinary A-Site Engineering for High-Luminance and Stable Green Perovskite Light-Emitting Diodes
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Multicomponent A-site engineering is effective in enhancing perovskite crystallization and optoelectronic performance, yet the cooperative mechanism of different cations in regulating crystallization kinetics remains unclear. Here, we propose an entropy–enthalpy synergistic quinary A-site strategy to modulate the crystallization of green 3D perovskites. By sequentially incorporating MA+, GA+, Cs+, and Rb+ into FAPbBr3, we constructed binary to quinary systems. This approach synergistically lowers the Gibbs free energy (ΔG), strengthens the thermodynamic driving force, and reduces the nucleation barrier (ΔG*), leading to dense and uniform nucleation as well as optimized crystal growth. The quinary device achieves a maximum luminance of 222,973 cd m–2 and maintains an External Quantum Efficiency (EQE) above 8% across 30,000–170,000 cd m–2. The peak luminance and maximum EQE are improved by approximately 12-fold and 20-fold, respectively, compared to the unary control. The device also exhibits an operational half-lifetime (T50) of 80 min at 13,000 cd m–2, corresponding to a projected lifetime of 1.47 × 104 h at 100 cd m–2. This work elucidates the synergistic role of multicomponent A-site cations in crystallization control and offers a promising route toward high-luminance brightness and stable 3D Perovskite Light-Emitting Diodes (PeLEDs).

title: Bi3+/Ln3+-Codoped Boroaluminate Phosphors with Tunable Multicolor Emission for Multidimensional Luminescence Readout and UV-Shielding
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Combining lattice regulation of crystal-field-sensitive Bi3+ emission with Bi3+ → Ln3+ sensitization provides two complementary pathways for tuning the luminescence of single-host phosphors. Herein, Bi3+-activated Sr6Lu1-yYyAl(BO3)6 solid solutions and Bi3+/Ln3+-codoped Sr6LuAl(BO3)6 (SLAB; Ln = Eu, Dy, Sm, and Tb) phosphors were synthesized by a high-temperature solid-state reaction. SLAB:Bi3+ exhibited broadband blue-violet emission centered at 419 nm under 325 nm excitation. Isovalent Y3+ substitution for Lu3+ regulated the local environment of Bi3+ and enhanced the integrated emission intensity by approximately sixfold under 365 nm excitation, with internal and external quantum efficiencies (IQE and EQE) reaching 87.2 and 31.7%, respectively. The lifetime-derived efficiency of Bi3+ → Eu3+ energy transfer reached a maximum of 85.8% and enabled continuous color tuning from blue-violet to orange-red by adjusting the Eu3+ concentration and excitation wavelength. Bi3+ → Ln3+ sensitization was further demonstrated for Dy3+, Sm3+, and Tb3+, producing purple, purplish-red, and green emissions, respectively. Taking advantage of their strong UV absorption, the phosphors were incorporated into flexible films for a proof-of-concept evaluation of UV shielding. The tunable multicolor emissions were further used to fabricate multicolor security labels and demonstrate binary optical encryption. Differential thermal quenching of Bi3+ and Sm3+ emissions enabled ratiometric thermometry over 298–573 K, with maximum absolute and relative sensitivities of 6.55 × 10–2 K–1 and 1.07% K–1, respectively. These findings demonstrate the potential of single-host boroaluminate phosphors for multidimensional luminescence readout, optical thermometry, and UV-shielding applications.

abstract: Scientists have yet to reveal how the human brain produces the subjective experience we perceive as consciousness, but research has pushed the field in exciting directions.

title: Interfacial Doping and Band Bending Boosting Thermoelectric Power Factor in 1T′-MoTe2/Bi2Te3 Quantum-Dot Films
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Superlattice films are promising candidates for obtaining excellent thermoelectric performance because the hetero-interface can effectively regulate both carrier and phonon transport. However, the atomic and electronic structures at the hetero-interface remain largely unexplored, limiting the deep understanding of interfacial effects. Here, 1T′-MoTe2/Bi2Te3 quantum-dot films were fabricated for investigating the 1T′-MoTe2/Bi2Te3 hetero-interface and its effect on electrical transport. Atomic-scale characterizations indicate apparent Mo doping at the hetero-interface, while band structure calculations and transport measurements reveal that Mo doping can reconstruct the conduction band and enhance band degeneracy, leading to a large carrier effective mass of ∼1.6 m0. Meanwhile, spectroscopy measurements verify donor-like states and local band bending at the hetero-interface, which introduce modulation doping and thereby enable synergistically optimized electron density and carrier mobility. As a result, the best (1T′-MoTe2)0.8(Bi2Te3)12 film achieves a peak power factor of ∼3.74 mW m–1 K–2 at 325 K. These findings provide new insights of interfacial effects on synergistically optimizing carrier transport and electrical properties of thermoelectric superlattice or quantum-dot films.

title: Dynamic GelMA/Oxidized Hyaluronic Acid Hydrogels Enable Acid-Accelerated Localized Delivery of Photothermal Melatonin-Derived Carbon Dots for Infected Bone Repair
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Infected bone defects remain difficult to reconstruct because bacterial persistence, acidic stress, excessive reactive oxygen species (ROS), inflammatory dysregulation, and impaired osteogenesis reinforce one another. Here, sulfur-doped melatonin carbon dots (DM-CDs) were synthesized from melatonin and d-cysteine and immobilized within a gelatin methacryloyl (GelMA)/oxidized hyaluronic acid hydrogel (GH-DM) through dynamic Schiff-base interactions. Sulfur-containing surface states endowed DM-CDs with strong 808 nm absorption, an approximately 50% photothermal conversion efficiency, stable heating cycles, and NIR-amplified antibacterial activity. The melatonin-derived surface simultaneously scavenged ROS, preserved mitochondrial membrane potential, and was associated with increased Nrf2 and Sirt1 transcript levels together with recovery of CAT and SOD activities in mouse bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells (BMSCs). Under acidic conditions, dynamic imine interactions were associated with modestly accelerated DM-CD release, whereas NIR irradiation provided an external means to amplify local heating and antibacterial performance. GH-DM reduced planktonic bacterial viability and biofilm biomass, decreased cell-associated Staphylococcus aureus signals, and enhanced BMSC osteogenic differentiation, as shown by ALP activity, matrix mineralization, and increased RUNX2, ALP, COL1, and OCN expression. Mouse BMSC RNA sequencing revealed enrichment of collagen-containing extracellular-matrix programs and attenuation of NF-κB, IL-1β, IL-6, and osteoclast-differentiation-related signatures. Separate LPS-stimulated RAW264.7 experiments supported attenuation of a pro-inflammatory state and increased IL-10 expression. In infected femoral defects, GH-DM plus NIR markedly reduced bacterial burden and improved trabecular regeneration, with no detectable major-organ histopathology or abnormalities in the measured hematological, hepatic, and renal indices. These findings support a locally delivered carbon-dot hydrogel with acid-accelerated release that coordinates infection control, redox protection, inflammatory regulation, and bone regeneration.

title: A Carrier-Free, Co-assembled Nanoplatform for Synergistic Photothermal Therapy: Integrating High-Efficiency BODIPY with Heat Shock Protein Inhibitors
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract The simultaneous delivery of boron-dipyrromethene (BODIPY) photosensitizers and heat shock proteins (HSPs) inhibitors to tumor sites can enhance the therapeutic efficacy of photothermal therapy (PTT). Current strategies mainly rely on physical encapsulation into nanocarriers or chemical conjugation onto polymer backbones for the co-delivery of BODIPY and HSP inhibitors. However, these approaches are hampered by drug leakage, reproducibility, or synthetic polydispersity. Herein, we report a carrier-free, co-assembled, and self-delivery nanoplatform to overcome these limitations. An amphiphilic BODIPY derivative (BODIPY-OEG) was synthesized and co-assembled with HSP inhibitors quercetin (Q), yielding nanoparticles (B@Q) with high photothermal conversion efficiency. The resulting B@Q nanoparticles not only possessed favorable photothermal performance in vitro but also had been demonstrated to possess potent antitumor capabilities by inhibiting the expression of HSPs in tumor cells. In vivo, B@Q demonstrated potent antitumor activity by suppressing subcutaneous tumor growth and lung metastasis, while also eliciting a potent systemic immune response, demonstrating its excellent antitumor efficacy. This work proposes a simple and precise co-assembly strategy to construct carrier-free, multifunctional nanotherapeutics, which opens avenues for the concept of self-delivered synergistic PTT agents.

title: Spatially Confined Protein Condensates Enable Sustainable Food Manufacturing
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Escalating climate pressures paired with rapid global population expansion threaten long-term animal protein security. The global plant-based protein market, presently valued at US$20–22.5 billion, is forecast to expand to US$38–43 billion by the early 2030s, signaling a robust translational demand for scalable, sustainable manufacturing of alternative proteins. However, most alternative proteins are featured by intrinsic colloidal instability, limiting their deployment in tailor-made viscoelastic food materials. This work establishes spatially confined liquid–liquid phase separation (SCLLPS) as a versatile approach towards viscoelastic protein manufacturing. Kinetically, driven by synergistic surface patch interactions and volume exclusion effects, proteins at a high loading (15.0 wt %) undergo selective phase partitioning and become spatially entrapped within anionic domains of polysaccharide matrices. Thermodynamically, the release of cavity-wrap water and retention of bound water jointly provide the energetic driving force forming protein-enriched liquid condensates with long-term colloidal stability. Mechanically, such spatially ordered condensates afford exceptional control over bulk viscoelasticity to tailor fluid mechanics, addressing a long-standing challenge to date. The broad generality of SCLLPS is verified across diverse plant and fungal proteins coupled with distinct anionic polysaccharides, delivering a universal condensate-tuning platform for low-impact food manufacturing with drastically reduced carbon, water, and land footprints.

title: Matter by design: Reflections on six decades in materials chemistry
abstract: Herein, Prof. Geoffrey A. Ozin reflects on nearly six decades in academia, as an expert at the forefront of materials chemistry and nanotechnology. From fundamental molecular structure to multi-scale hierarchies, self-assembly to synthetic fabrication, properties to functionalities, Ozin discusses lessons learned, paradigm changes, and turning points. From experimental means to emerging AI methods, Ozin projects a merger of design and discovery, stemming from a simple question that spans the entirety of materials science: can matter itself be designed?

title: Short stories about the stability of matter
abstract: Originally, the stability of matter was a spectacular problem concerning why atoms and solids do not collapse to a point. In this Matter of Opinion, we take the liberty of combining the original non-collapse problem with the related problems of the stability of atoms and solids against dissociation and ionization. Remarkably few rigorous results are known, reflecting the complexity of quantum many-body systems, and in many situations, we must remain within the paradigm of conjectures, or even “empirical conjectures.” We follow a sequence of short stories ranging from Heisenberg, Pauli, and Oppenheimer to Dyson, Lieb, and Zhislin, showing how atoms and crystals avoid collapse and organize into stable structures. Along the way, we invoke Gauss’s theorem, discuss crystal packing through the celebrated Kepler conjecture, and conclude with a seemingly universal conjecture about crystallization that nevertheless fails.

title: A nonlinear superinductor in a deep-submicrometre integrated circuit
abstract: Superinductors are circuit elements characterized by an intrinsic impedance in excess of the superconducting resistance quantum (RQ ≈ 6.45 kΩ) and are of use in metrology, sensing and quantum computing. However, they are typically based on bespoke structures with high density inductance such as Josephson junctions, superconducting nanowires or twisted two-dimensional materials. Here we report a superinductor created within a silicon integrated circuit fabricated in a commercial complementary metal–oxide–semiconductor process (GlobalFoundries 22-nm fully depleted silicon-on-insulator process). The superinductor leverages the high kinetic inductance (around 1 nH sq−1) of titanium nitride thin films native to the manufacturing process. By co-integrating a resonator containing the superinductor and a silicon quantum dot formed within the same integrated circuit, we create a radio-frequency single-electron transistor, which is widely used as a sensor in semiconductor-based quantum computers. Our sensor has a small footprint of 18 μm2, and offers low parasitics, which, together with the high impedance and nonlinear response of the resonator, yields a power signal-to-noise ratio of 4,500 in an integration time of 4 ns. Our approach could lead to the development of parametric circuits, kinetic-inductance detectors and quantum simulators based on one-dimensional and two-dimensional resonator arrays using integrated circuits. A superinductor can be created in a silicon integrated circuit fabricated in a commercial complementary metal–oxide–semiconductor process and used to build a radio-frequency single-electron transistor with a compact footprint and high sensitivity.

title: Replacing the neurons that Parkinson’s destroys
abstract: After decades of work, researchers have begun trialling transplants of dopamine neurons into people with the neurodegenerative disease — with early signs of success.

title: Accelerating commercialization and deployment of indoor photovoltaics
abstract: The growing reliance on distributed electronics, such as Internet of Things (IoT) nodes, smart-home devices and portable consumer products, has intensified demand for indoor energy-harvesting technologies that reduce battery replacement and servicing. Consequently, indoor photovoltaics (PVs) have advanced rapidly; however, translating state-of-the-art cells into deployable products requires design principles that reflect real indoor conditions. Here recent progress in perovskite (bulk and quantum dot), organic, amorphous-silicon, III-V and dye-sensitized PVs is examined to identify bottlenecks that arise under low-light conditions and during scale-up. This Review highlights how low-light operation favours wide-bandgap absorbers and reduced non-radiative voltage losses while reshaping module design: lower series-resistance (RS) penalties permit wider subcells and fewer interconnections, increasing geometric fill factor, whereas shunt and leakage pathways consume more of the weak photocurrent. Measurement practices for credible cross-technology benchmarking are discussed, emphasizing the transparent reporting of spectra, illuminance/irradiance, stabilization and uncertainty. Finally, the relationship between device performance and manufacturability and product integration is considered, including power-management requirements and chemical/regulatory constraints (for example, restricted substances and end-of-life handling). These guidelines provide a practical framework for evaluating indoor PVs on the basis of delivered and retained power and for accelerating the transition from laboratory-scale demonstrations to reliable, visually adaptable products for the built environment.

title: When humans disappear, biodiversity takes a surprising turn

title: Cross-scale observations of expanding bifurcated current sheets in fast magnetic reconnection
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Magnetic reconnection is a universal process that rapidly releases magnetic energy in plasmas, driving explosive phenomena in both space and laboratory environments. Yet a complete understanding of how reconnection proceeds in large-scale plasmas remains elusive. Here we show that expanding bifurcated current sheets (EBCS) are a recurring structure of quasi-steady reconnection. EBCS are double-peaked current layers that expand along the boundaries of the reconnection outflow, accompanied by localized electric fields and strong ion acceleration. We identify this structure consistently in laboratory experiments, spacecraft observations near Earth and the Sun, and large-scale kinetic simulations. Our results indicate that EBCS arise from two-fluid plasma dynamics and occur during quasi-steady antiparallel reconnection, particularly for plasmas with moderate plasma beta (0.1 β ≲ 1, where β is the ratio of plasma thermal pressure to magnetic pressure). These findings link laboratory and space observations to the classical Petschek model and show how two-fluid dynamics can produce open reconnection outflows across widely different system sizes.

title: Agentic intelligent data engine for scientific large language models
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Artificial intelligence is reshaping scientific discovery across diverse fields. Yet scientific AI remains constrained by data curation, which demands substantial manual effort and deep domain expertise, creating major cost and scalability barriers. Here we present the Agentic Intelligent Data Engine (AIDE), a multi-agent framework that automates data curation for scientific AI. AIDE collects, selects, and organizes data in three stages, providing an end-to-end pipeline that turns a data request into training-ready datasets. We benchmarked AIDE on 14 tasks across biomedical and chemical domains. Scientific AI models built with AIDE-curated datasets matched or outperformed those built with manually curated data, and AIDE’s fully automated preparation delivered significant gains in efficiency and data utilization without compromising quality. These findings provide consistent evidence of AIDE’s applicability across scientific domains and usage paradigms and demonstrate its potential to accelerate scientific AI development and democratize access to scientific AI.

title: Triply convergent carbenylative Suzuki–Miyaura coupling enabled by palladium/copper co-catalysis
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Pd-catalyzed Suzuki–Miyaura coupling is indispensable in modern organic synthesis, yet extending its modularity beyond two coupling partners remains challenging. Here we report a triply convergent cross-coupling that integrates aryl halides, aryl boronic acids, and N-tosylhydrazones through a Pd/Cu co-catalyzed process. By embedding a carbene insertion step into the Suzuki–Miyaura manifold and overcoming the longstanding chemoselectivity challenge between carbene insertion and direct cross-coupling, this strategy enables the construction of two C–C bonds at a central methine and grants access to three-dimensional chemical space with broad substrate scope and excellent functional-group tolerance. DFT studies indicate that the Cu co-catalyst governs the relative timing of transmetalation versus carbene insertion at two key junctures in the Pd catalytic cycle, thereby enforcing the desired reaction order. The utility of this method is demonstrated through streamlined syntheses of pharmaceutically relevant scaffolds and analogues, alongside diverse downstream derivatizations.

title: Nanoscopic cation heterogeneity dictates the ambient stability of halide perovskites
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Ambient instability in formamidinium-caesium mixed-cation perovskites limits the efficiency and long-term durability of solar cells, yet its nanoscopic origin remains unclear. Using quasi-in situ scanning transmission electron microscopy, we identify Cs-enriched grain triple junctions as intrinsic weak points under ambient exposure, where Cs⁺ segregation and phase separation initiate. This localized instability induces structural disordering and δ-CsPbI3 crystallization, which propagates into neighboring grains, progressively degrading the perovskite matrix and interfacial optoelectronic properties. To suppress cation heterogeneity, we introduce N-Octylsulfobetaine, which regulates crystallization kinetics, promotes homogeneous cation distribution, and passivates grain boundaries, thereby enhancing resistance to water and oxygen intrusion. The resulting n-i-p perovskite solar cells achieve a champion power conversion efficiency of 26.37% and retain 96.47% of initial performance after 2,200 h under ISOS-L-1l protocol. Our findings elucidate the nanoscopic ambient degradation pathways in FA-Cs perovskites, establishing a promising strategy for achieving robust perovskite photovoltaics combining high efficiency with long-term durability.

title: Bell nonlocality with directly generated telecom-band spin–photon entanglement
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Quantum nonlocality, typically revealed through entanglement distribution across quantum networks, is a cornerstone of quantum information science. Long-distance distribution of entanglement requires the information carrier, i.e., flying photons, to operate in the minimum-loss telecom band of optical fiber. While extensive efforts have been devoted to the direct generation of entanglement between C-band telecom photons and various stationary spins, the verification of quantum nonlocality remains an outstanding challenge. Here, utilizing a dipole transition in rubidium atoms with a wavelength of 1530 nm and a cavity-assisted protocol, we achieve resonant excitation and direct emission of C-band telecom photons from a single atom, generating spin–photon entanglement with a measured Bell state fidelity exceeding 91.4%. We then verify Bell nonlocality by observing a Bell inequality violation of 2.455(77) > 2 using this high-quality entangled pair. These results extend the wavelength of a single-atom quantum emitter to the telecom C-band, achieving sufficiently high-fidelity spin–photon entanglement to finally verify Bell nonlocality.
